% Converted, ltx-talk, C-ONSLIDE-ARG workaround NOT applied -- the defect.
%
% This is the conversion that looks right: \onslide<2>{...} is correct Beamer, so it survives a
% mechanical conversion untouched and nothing complains. Under ltx-talk \onslide is declared
% { D <> { all } } with no +m, so this parses as the DECLARATION \onslide<2> followed by a
% stray brace group -- and the declaration blanks everything to the end of the frame.
%
% Measured on ltx-talk 0.6.2 / TeX Live 2026, lualatex, two passes, against after.tex, whose
% only difference is \uncover in place of \onslide. Non-white fraction of the prose band
% (0.05,0.35)-(0.75,0.62) at 70dpi:
%
%                       pages  Tagged  overlay 1  overlay 2  text layer
%   after.tex (\uncover)    2     yes     0.0387     0.0595   identical
%   this file  (\onslide)   2     yes     0.0000     0.0595   identical
%
% Overlay 1 is EMPTY -- including the prose that has nothing to do with the overlay and must be
% visible on every page. Overlay 2 is pixel-for-pixel what the fixed version produces, so a
% reader flicking to the last page of the frame sees nothing wrong.
%
% The text layers are byte-identical, checked with diff: ltx-talk typesets every overlay branch
% once and toggles visibility with OCG layers, so pdftotext returns the hidden text too. That is
% why this fixture measures pixels. One 11-deck course had 139 of these sites; a 20-deck course
% another 204.
\DocumentMetadata{lang=en, pdfversion=2.0, pdfstandard={a-4,ua-2}, tagging=on}
\documentclass{ltx-talk}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}
\onslide<2>{Revealed on the second overlay.}

Prose that must stay visible on every overlay, including the first.
\end{frame}
\end{document}
